name: Tarpon Springs
title: Mobile boat mechanics in Tarpon Springs, FL
intro: Home base. Tarpon Springs boats live on the Anclote River, in the canals off Whitcomb Bayou and Lake Tarpon, and on trailers headed for Anclote River Park and Fred Howard Park. Mechanics in the network reach anywhere in town within the hour.
waters: Anclote River and the Sponge Docks
Anclote Key and the Gulf flats
Whitcomb Bayou and Spring Bayou canals
ramps: Anclote River Park (public ramp, Baillies Bluff Rd)
Craig Park on Spring Bayou (small boats)
boats: Flats and bay boats, Gulf center consoles, pontoons on Lake Tarpon, sailboats and trawlers along the river, commercial sponge and shrimp boats.
issues: Shallow-water prop and skeg damage on the Anclote flats
Corrosion on lift-kept boats a quarter mile from the Gulf
Ethanol fuel problems on boats that sit through summer

faqs.q: Do you come to the Sponge Docks and the river marinas?
faqs.a: Yes. Mechanics carry insurance certificates for the marinas that require them.

faqs.q: How fast can someone get to Tarpon?
faqs.a: Same day for most calls; emergencies at the ramp are handled by whoever is closest.

name: Palm Harbor and Ozona
title: Mobile boat mechanics in Palm Harbor and Ozona, FL
intro: Ozona and the Palm Harbor waterfront sit on St. Joseph Sound behind Honeymoon and Caladesi Islands. Most boats here are on lifts behind homes or in the small marinas off Orange Street, which is exactly where mobile service makes sense.
waters: Honeymoon Island and the Dunedin Pass
boats: Bay boats and center consoles on lifts, pontoons, kayaks and skiffs out of Ozona.
issues: Lift-kept boats with corroded grounds and dead batteries
Trim and tilt problems from boats raised and lowered daily
Water pumps on engines idled through the no-wake zones

faqs.q: Can you service a boat in the Ozona marinas?
faqs.a: Yes, with the marina's permission and an insurance certificate on file.

name: Dunedin
title: Mobile boat mechanics in Dunedin, FL
intro: Dunedin's marina, the causeway to Honeymoon Island, and the canal neighborhoods along the Intracoastal make it one of the busiest boating towns in Pinellas. Mechanics in the network service boats at the city marina, on private lifts, and at the causeway ramp.
waters: St. Joseph Sound and the Intracoastal
boats: Center consoles, pontoons, sailboats at the marina, dinghies and skiffs for the islands.
issues: Sandbar and shallow-pass prop damage
Batteries and charging on weekend boats
Fuel problems after the summer lull

faqs.q: Do you work at Dunedin Marina?
faqs.a: Yes. Mechanics in the network already service slip holders there.

name: Clearwater and the beaches
title: Mobile boat mechanics in Clearwater, Clearwater Beach, Largo and Belleair, FL
intro: Clearwater Harbor, the Clearwater Beach marina, Island Estates canals, and the Intracoastal down through Belleair and Largo hold thousands of boats on lifts and in slips. The Seminole Boat Ramp is one of the busiest public ramps on the Gulf coast. Mechanics in the network cover all of it.
waters: Intracoastal Waterway south to the Narrows
boats: Offshore center consoles, charter and dive boats at the beach marina, cruisers, sailboats, pontoons, personal watercraft.
issues: Heavy-use charter and rental engines needing frequent service
Slip-kept cruisers with manifold, riser, and bellows wear
Electronics upgrades on offshore boats

faqs.q: Can you meet me at the Seminole ramp?
faqs.a: Yes for a boat that won't start at the ramp; call rather than post, so the nearest mechanic can head over.
Yes. Several mechanics in the network do commercial work and understand the schedule pressure.

name: Safety Harbor and Oldsmar
title: Mobile boat mechanics in Safety Harbor and Oldsmar, FL
intro: The top of Old Tampa Bay is quieter water with a lot of lift-kept bay boats and pontoons behind homes in Safety Harbor, Oldsmar, and the east side of Palm Harbor. Philippe Park and R.E. Olds Park are the launch points.
ramps: R.E. Olds Park and Mobbly Bayou (Oldsmar)
boats: Bay boats, pontoons, deck boats, jon boats for the bay flats.
issues: Shallow, grassy flats that foul water pickups: overheat alarms
Engines run at idle for long no-wake stretches: carbon and plugs
Trailers from boats launched at Philippe Park

faqs.q: Why does my engine overheat on Old Tampa Bay?
faqs.a: Grass and silt in the water pickup is the usual cause up here. A pump and thermostat check on the lift sorts it out.

name: St. Petersburg and Gulfport
title: Mobile boat mechanics in St. Petersburg, Gulfport and the Pinellas beaches, FL
intro: St. Petersburg is the sailing and cruising capital of the bay: the Municipal Marina, the Harborage, Maximo Marina, Gulfport Marina, Tierra Verde, and the canals of Shore Acres, Snell Isle, and Coquina Key. Diesel, inboard, and electrical specialists in the network live here.
waters: Tampa Bay and the downtown waterfront
Boca Ciega Bay and the beaches
Fort De Soto and Egmont Key
ramps: Fort De Soto Park (24 lanes, park fee)
boats: Sailboats and trawlers in the marinas, express cruisers, offshore and bay center consoles, flats boats in the south county.
issues: Diesel and inboard service backlogs at the yards
Storm-damaged boats still being brought back after Helene and Milton
Electrical and systems work on live-aboards and cruisers

faqs.q: Do you work at the Municipal Marina and the Harborage?
faqs.a: Yes, with insurance certificates on file where required.

faqs.q: Can you do a pre-purchase mechanical inspection?
faqs.a: Yes. It is one of the most requested jobs downtown, especially on sailboat diesels.

name: Tampa
title: Mobile boat mechanics in Tampa, FL: Davis Islands, South Tampa, Ballast Point, Town 'n' Country
intro: Tampa's boats are spread between Davis Islands and the downtown marinas, the canals of South Tampa and Ballast Point, the Hillsborough River, and the Rocky Point and Town 'n' Country side of Old Tampa Bay. Hillsborough mechanics in the network cover the city.
waters: Old Tampa Bay and Rocky Point
The Gandy and Courtney Campbell corridors
boats: Center consoles and bay boats, cruisers at Marjorie Park and the downtown marinas, river pontoons, wake boats.
issues: Slip-kept inboards needing annual service
Electrical faults on older cruisers
Wake boat ballast and engine service

faqs.a: Yes, inboard mechanics in the network do routine service and ballast systems; some warranty items go to the dealer.

name: Apollo Beach and Ruskin
title: Mobile boat mechanics in Apollo Beach, Ruskin and Sun City Center, FL
intro: South Hillsborough is lift country: miles of canals in Apollo Beach, MiraBay, and Symphony Isles, the Little Manatee River out of Ruskin, and the big public ramps at E.G. Simmons and Williams Park. Mobile service is the only kind that makes sense here.
waters: Cockroach Bay and the south shore flats
ramps: Apollo Beach boat ramp (Apollo Beach Blvd)
boats: Bay boats and center consoles on lifts, flats skiffs, pontoons, a growing number of larger offshore boats in MiraBay.
issues: Boats that sit on lifts through summer: fuel and battery no-starts in fall
Corrosion on engines a few feet above brackish canal water
Trailer failures on ramp boats from Sun City Center and Wimauma

faqs.q: Can you get to MiraBay and Symphony Isles?
faqs.a: Yes. Give the gate the mechanic's name when we text it to you.

faqs.q: I'm in Sun City Center with a trailer boat. Do you come there?
faqs.a: Yes, driveway service for trailer boats is routine.

name: New Port Richey and Port Richey
title: Mobile boat mechanics in New Port Richey, Port Richey and Holiday, FL
intro: The Pithlachascotee River, the Gulf Harbors and Flor-A-Mar canals, and the Pasco coast flats are trailer-boat and lift-boat territory. Pasco mechanics in the network serve the whole coast from Holiday to Hudson.
waters: Pasco coast flats and the Anclote Keys
Durney Key and the near-shore islands
boats: Bay boats, flats skiffs, pontoons, airboats, kayaks; a strong scallop-season fleet.
issues: Shallow coast and oyster bars: props, skegs, and lower units
Scallop season (July to September) crowds and breakdowns
Trailer bearings from frequent ramp launches

faqs.q: My lower unit hit bottom on the flats. Can you check it?
faqs.a: Yes: gear oil check for water and metal, prop shaft runout, and a pressure test. Catching it early is the difference between a seal and a rebuild.

name: Hudson and Bayonet Point
title: Mobile boat mechanics in Hudson, Bayonet Point and Aripeka, FL
intro: Hudson's canal neighborhoods, Hudson Beach, the SunWest area, and the Aripeka backwaters are the north end of our coverage. It is a long way from any dealer, which is why owners up here wait weeks for shop service and why a mobile mechanic matters.
waters: Hudson Channel and the Gulf flats
boats: Flats skiffs, bay boats, pontoons, airboats, and a big scallop-season crowd.
issues: Long channel runs at idle: fouled plugs and carbon
Groundings on the limestone flats
Older engines and legacy two-strokes needing experienced mechanics

faqs.q: Do you come as far as Aripeka and Hernando Beach?
faqs.a: Aripeka, yes. Hernando Beach depends on the mechanic; ask and we'll tell you honestly.
